basics.description:
Deploy **UTL-X Transformation Engine — Professional** into your Azure subscription.

**Professional plan:** one engine instance, 4 vCPU and up to 8 GB. Hosts 50+ integrations, messages of 1 MB and above.

Billing is handled automatically through your Azure bill. A 14-day free trial is included.

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: Azure region for all resources. Choose a region close to your workloads.

options.text: [concat('Suggested admin key (copy this): **', guid(), '**  — Paste it into the Admin API Key field below and save it in a password manager. You can also choose your own key (minimum 12 characters).')]

elements.name: adminKey
elements.toolTip: Protects the Admin API and Web UI. Use the suggested UUID above, or enter your own (minimum 12 characters). Save it securely — it cannot be retrieved after deployment.

constraints.validationMessage: The admin key must be at least 12 characters.

elements.name: dataPlaneKey
elements.toolTip: Protects the HTTP data path that applications post messages to. A SEPARATE key from the admin key on purpose: an application holding this one can run your transformations but cannot deploy, delete, or list them. Minimum 12 characters. Save it securely — it cannot be retrieved after deployment.

constraints.validationMessage: The data path key must be at least 12 characters.

options.text: Two keys, two jobs. The *admin* key manages transformations through the Web UI and Admin API. The *data path* key lets an application POST a message to /api/transformations/{id}/run and get the transformed result back — nothing else. Use different values: whichever one leaks, the other still holds.

Save this key securely — it is stored as a Container App secret and cannot be read back after deployment. To change it: az containerapp secret set --name <app> -g <rg> --secrets admin-key=<new-key>, then restart the container.

Professional plan: one engine instance with 4 vCPU and up to 8 GB of memory, processing up to 8 messages at a time. Transforms JSON, XML, CSV, YAML, and OData natively with 650+ stdlib functions, schema validation, and pipeline chaining. Twice the CPU and twice the JVM heap of Starter, so each message is transformed faster and large payloads fit. Ideal for production workloads with multiple integration flows.

elements.name: instanceSize
elements.label: Instance size
elements.toolTip: Total CPU and memory for the instance. Azure allows only fixed CPU/memory pairs, so these are chosen together rather than separately. The figure shown is the whole instance; the admin UI sidecar takes 0.25 vCPU and 0.5 GB of it.

options.text: XML and JSON messages expand 10-50x in memory during transformation (UDM parsing). Up to 8 messages are transformed at a time, so memory usage scales with the largest message you expect. For messages over 500 KB, use 8 GB.

elements.name: minReplicas
elements.label: Always-on instance
elements.toolTip: 1 keeps the single instance running. 0 lets it scale to zero when idle, which costs nothing but adds a cold start (JVM boot plus bundle compile) to the first message.

options.text: Without persistent storage the engine keeps transformations in memory only: they are lost on every restart and must be re-uploaded through the Admin API. Enabling it mounts an Azure Files share at /utlxe/data, so uploads survive restarts — and a .utlar bundle placed on the share starts the engine in locked mode, where transformations come from CI/CD and the Admin API refuses changes.

elements.name: enablePersistentStorage
elements.label: Persistent storage
elements.toolTip: Creates a Standard_LRS storage account and a 100 GiB file share in this resource group, mounted at /utlxe/data.

allowedValues.label: Disabled — in-memory only, re-upload after every restart

options.text:
Two ways in, and they are not exclusive.

HTTP: applications POST a document to /api/transformations/{id}/run with the data path key and receive the transformed result in the response. The body is the document itself — XML, JSON, CSV, YAML — with Content-Type saying which. This path is always available.

Azure Service Bus: UTLXe also consumes from a queue you own and publishes results to a topic you own, with auto-scaling driven by queue depth. Choose it here to have the deployment wire that up for you.

elements.name: messagingMode
elements.label: How messages reach UTLXe
elements.toolTip: HTTP: applications POST a document to the published data path with the data path key and receive the transformed result in the response. Azure Service Bus: the engine consumes from a queue you own and publishes results to a topic you own. Service Bus deployments keep the HTTP data path as well — this choice decides whether a Service Bus source is wired up, not whether HTTP works.
elements.defaultValue: HTTP — applications POST a document, get the result back

allowedValues.label: HTTP — applications POST a document, get the result back
Azure Service Bus — queue in, topic out

elements.name: serviceBusConnection
elements.toolTip: A connection string for your Service Bus namespace with Send and Listen rights. The namespace, queue and topic must already exist — this offer does not create them.

constraints.validationMessage: Paste the full connection string, starting with Endpoint=sb://

elements.name: inputQueueName
elements.label: Input queue name
elements.toolTip: The existing queue UTLXe consumes from.

elements.name: outputTopicName
elements.label: Output topic name
elements.toolTip: The existing topic UTLXe publishes transformed messages to.

options.text: Name your transformation 'servicebus-input' when you upload it. Messages arriving on the queue are routed to the transformation whose name matches the input binding, so a differently named transformation leaves messages consumed but not transformed.

Publish transformed messages to an Azure Event Hub instead of the Service Bus topic. Output only: consuming FROM an Event Hub needs a Dapr checkpoint store and an Event Hubs scaling trigger, which this release does not configure. Requires a message source to be selected above.

elements.name: enableEventHubs
elements.label: Publish results to an Event Hub
elements.toolTip: When enabled, transformed messages go to the Event Hub below rather than the Service Bus topic.

elements.name: eventHubConnection
elements.toolTip: Namespace-level connection string with Send rights, from Shared access policies on your Event Hubs namespace.

constraints.validationMessage: Paste the Event Hubs namespace connection string; it starts with Endpoint=sb://

elements.name: outputEventHub
elements.label: Output Event Hub name
elements.toolTip: The Event Hub (entity) inside the namespace that results are published to.

constraints.validationMessage: 1-50 characters: letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore.
